findings.title: canManage() grants management rights to callers that only have VIEW scope on groups
getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses the resource's internal id instead of the group's id, breaking per-group view filtering
findings.body: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), for each group-type Resource found, the code calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and adds groupResource.getId() to the granted set. However, resources created for groups via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() store the actual GroupModel id in resource.getName() (see resolveGroup()), not in resource.getId() (which is the authorization store's own generated identifier for the Resource entity). All other methods in this class (canView(GroupModel), canManage(GroupModel), canViewMembers, canManageMembers, canManageMembership) correctly pass group.getId() which matches resource.getName(). Because hasPermission()'s internal lookup does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), passing the resource's own id instead of its name will almost never find the resource, so permission checks for individual groups silently fail and fall back to the (usually absent) all-groups permission. Additionally, even where hasPermission did succeed, the method would return the wrong identifiers (resource ids, not group ids) in the resulting Set<String>. Since this set is used by UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource to filter the user search by group membership (session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)), real group ids never show up there, so admins granted per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions will not see any users through this path, defeating the feature added by this PR (the exact scenario covered by GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest#testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers / testCanViewUserByManageGroupMembers).

findings.title: No negative test ensures VIEW-only group permission cannot perform management actions
findings.body: testManageAllGroups() only exercises the case where the policy is granted the MANAGE scope and verifies group creation/management succeeds. There is no test that grants only the VIEW scope for all-groups (or a specific group) and asserts that management actions (create group, add child, map roles) are forbidden. Given the canManage() bug in GroupPermissionsV2 (treats VIEW as sufficient for MANAGE), such a negative test would have caught the privilege-escalation regression before merge.

findings.title: getResourceName() has no special-cased display for Groups (or Clients) resource type
findings.body: getResourceName() special-cases USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE to resolve a friendly name ("All users" or the username) for display purposes (e.g. in the admin console permission UI). No equivalent handling was added for the newly introduced GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE (or for CLIENTS), so for group-scoped permissions the method falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which for individually-scoped group permissions is the raw group UUID (the resource name) rather than a human-readable group name/path. This is inconsistent with the Users handling added in the same method and will show opaque IDs instead of group names wherever this helper is used to render permission resource names.
